item.text: {"text":"Recent research supports testing history dependence through complementary perturbations. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) reports that excessive recent-item emphasis can hurt accuracy. [FCESR (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13632) distinguishes sufficiency—whether a retained subsequence preserves a recommendation—from necessity—whether removing it changes the recommendation. [Demystifying Sequential Recommendations (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal history edits that change recommendations. These methods assess model dependence; their results do not establish that influential interactions match users’ perceived intent. [Spotify’s 2026 benchmark study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) finds pairwise transition models outperforming reproduced Transformers on four of five benchmarks, motivating controls for popularity, recency and simple transitions before attributing gains to complex sequence reasoning.\n\nSuggested diagnostic synthesis: compare equal-size deletions of recent repeated interactions, older isolated interactions and randomly selected events; shuffle earlier history while preserving the last item, then separately perturb the last item. Define repetition using observed item IDs, and report unavailable cases rather than inventing repeated events. Measure target-rank changes and top-10 overlap alongside next-item HR@10 on training-prefix targets excluded from model fitting. Include last-item, order-insensitive history and positional-component ablations; distinguish inference-time component removal from retrained ablations. Match deletion counts, control padding and position shifts, repeat random perturbations, and report results by category and history length. Sensitivity accompanied by predictive degradation supports useful dependence; rank movement alone indicates instability. These are proposed controls, not established findings about the four RecHarness datasets, and cannot identify causal intent or unobserved user traits."}
